description: The shell uses a fixed shared-temp path `/tmp/.iplv.err` and `/tmp/.iplb.err` for capturing stderr from the python validate / launchctl bootstrap calls (lines 20-25, 79-87). On a multi-user macOS host (or one where /tmp is world-writable, which is the default), this is a TOCTOU symlink race: an unprivileged attacker who can win the race can pre-create `/tmp/.iplv.err` as a symlink to e.g. `~/.openclaw/state/cron-ledger.jsonl`, and the redirection `2>/tmp/.iplv.err` will silently truncate the target. Even without a malicious actor, two parallel invocations for two different slots (EDGE-E7 explicitly contemplates concurrent calls) will clobber each other's error file and report wrong stderr text to the user. Fix: use `mktemp -t iplv.XXXXXX` per-invocation, or capture stderr into a bash variable via process substitution.

evidence.snippet:
if ! ( cd "$SHARED_DIR" && "$PY" -m lib.plist_render validate "$SLOT" 2>/tmp/.iplv.err ); then
  echo "invalid slot: validation failed — $(cat /tmp/.iplv.err 2>/dev/null)" >&2
  rm -f /tmp/.iplv.err
  exit 3
fi
